title: Discovery of a magnetic monopole

concept.text: The innovation would be the reproducible discovery of a free particle carrying nonzero magnetic charge: an isolated source of magnetic field whose charge is a measurable particle property. Under the Dirac quantization condition used to define this target, that magnetic charge would be a nonzero integer multiple of the Dirac unit. Establishing the charge is central to the discovery; observing an unusual particle signal alone would leave the defining property unproven.

The target encompasses more than one theoretical possibility. Conventional grand-unified-theory monopoles could be extraordinarily massive, while other scenarios motivate searches at collider-accessible masses. Discovering magnetic charge would therefore open an experimental investigation of the particle's origin, mass, interactions and underlying theory. It would not, by itself, establish that the particle came from grand unification.

significance.text: A confirmed free monopole would establish magnetic charge as an observed particle property and give experimental substance to a longstanding extension of electromagnetism. Adding magnetic sources would make Maxwell's equations more symmetric between electricity and magnetism. Dirac's argument connects the existence of a monopole to the discreteness of electric charge, so discovery would provide a direct experimental handle on charge quantization. Measuring the minimum magnetic charge could also constrain the structure of the underlying gauge group.

These consequences would be fundamental even before a particular theory was identified. Monopoles occur in several theoretical settings, so a discovery would give theories containing them a concrete experimental target without uniquely selecting a grand-unified theory. Establishing the particle's theoretical origin would require additional measurements and comparison with competing predictions.

Some heavy grand-unified monopoles are predicted to catalyze nucleon decay through the Rubakov–Callan effect. Demonstrating that process would be a further discovery, with its own interaction and rate measurements; generic magnetic charge does not establish catalysis. Industrial uses remain speculative in this record, with no demonstrated application or justified practical forecast. Neither catalysis nor an application is required for the fundamental discovery to matter.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is a convincing positive measurement of a free particle's magnetic charge, together with reproducibility and adequate rejection of instrumental and particle backgrounds. The documented searches demonstrate ways to look for monopoles and constrain particular possibilities, but they do not supply that discovery measurement. This selected evidence also cannot establish the outcome of every monopole search through 1 November 2026.

Producing or encountering a monopole is a major physical barrier. The IceCube material describes conventional GUT-scale masses above 10^14 GeV, far beyond the reach of the collider scenario considered here. Masses and cosmic abundances depend on the theory and cosmological history; extreme rarity is not a universal prediction established by these sources. Collider searches face limits from available production energy, uncertain production rates and detector acceptance. Cosmic searches instead depend on the incoming flux and on the velocities and interactions to which the detector is sensitive.

The measurement problem is equally important. A trapping search needs a monopole to stop in material that can subsequently be scanned, and the induction detector must distinguish a stable magnetic-charge response from spurious current changes. A track-based search needs enough information, including independently constrained velocity, to distinguish magnetic charge from electrically charged backgrounds. Searches based on monopole-induced nucleon decay also depend on the assumed catalysis cross section; their sensitivity does not transfer automatically to monopoles lacking that interaction.

current_state.text: MoEDAL's 2024 search examined the CMS beam pipe for monopoles produced through the Schwinger effect and trapped in its material. It observed no monopole signal and reported 95% confidence-level exclusions reaching masses of 80 GeV, with its strongest comparative constraints covering magnetic charges from 2 to 45 Dirac units. These are exclusions within the paper's production and trapping assumptions, rather than a model-independent exclusion of every monopole in that mass and charge range. The supplied review reports complete text extraction of the seven-page paper. The research metadata gives 15 August 2024 as the journal publication date, but that exact date was not verified in the reviewed document contents.

The MoEDAL experiment also documents a concrete magnetic-charge measurement method: a trapped monopole passing through a superconducting induction detector would produce a persistent current proportional to its magnetic charge. Calibration and repeated scans are essential because spurious signals can occur, whereas a monopole should give a consistent response. This establishes an experimental route to the target observable, not a positive monopole detection.

The IceCube proceedings supplied as arXiv:2507.05896, dated 8 July 2025 in the research metadata, quote existing slow-monopole flux bounds of approximately 10^-17 to 10^-18 cm^-2 s^-1 sr^-1 at 90% confidence. Those bounds come from a previous analysis and depend on the assumed proton-decay catalysis cross section. The new analysis described in the proceedings was still under development, including training and development of its final event-selection stage; its projected sensitivity must therefore remain separate from completed exclusion results. Although the landing-page evidence was partial, the supplied review also used a complete eleven-page text extraction. No additional numerical result is inferred here from figures that the review did not inspect.

The supplied research additionally attributes limits for charges up to 10 Dirac units to MoEDAL's full-detector Run 2 paper and gives 20 February 2025 as its publication date. However, no document artifact for that citation was retained, so the supplied review could not verify its contents, detailed assumptions or exact date. The reported result remains an unverified part of this account; the access limitation does not establish that it is false.

Evidence limitation: the supplied research also reports a 2025 NOvA null search, but provides no corresponding source, so its scope and numerical results cannot be established here. More broadly, the supplied material contains no search record establishing comprehensive coverage through 1 November 2026. The documented results support specific null searches and an ongoing analysis; they do not justify a definitive statement about every experiment's discovery status at that date.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed completion criterion: reproducibly detect a free particle with nonzero magnetic charge consistent, within measured uncertainty, with a nonzero integer multiple of the Dirac unit. This is a proposed definition for this innovation, not a published consensus standard. The result should measure the defining magnetic charge and quantify its uncertainty, rather than infer a monopole solely from missing energy or an excess of highly ionizing tracks.
completion_criteria.label: Reproducible free-particle magnetic charge matches nonzero integer Dirac units

completion_criteria.text: One technically grounded route would be a trapped candidate producing a calibrated persistent-current response in a superconducting induction detector. Repeated scans should return the same magnetic-charge value, with calibration, instrumental artifacts and spurious responses addressed. The relevant observable is the persistent current proportional to magnetic charge; an ordinary trapped superconducting flux quantum alone would not meet this criterion.
completion_criteria.label: Repeated calibrated persistent-current scans yield consistent trapped-particle magnetic charge

completion_criteria.text: Proposed alternative route: a particle track with independently constrained velocity and a sufficiently informative detector response to measure magnetic charge and distinguish it from electrically charged backgrounds. Strong ionization would be useful evidence, but would need the additional information that makes the magnetic-charge interpretation discriminating. Reproducibility could involve repeated measurements of a trapped particle, additional consistent events, independent apparatus, or a combination appropriate to the detection method.
completion_criteria.label: Velocity-constrained tracks measure magnetic charge and distinguish electrically charged backgrounds

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundary: a convincing discovery report should specify the demonstrated charge range, mass information, velocity range, detector acceptance, interaction assumptions and remaining alternatives. Independent confirmation would strengthen the conclusion. Finite tests would establish the discovery and its measured properties within those conditions; they would not establish every possible monopole species, a unique grand-unified origin, nucleon-decay catalysis or practical utility.
completion_criteria.label: Discovery report specifies measured properties, detection conditions and remaining alternatives

related_concepts.text: PHY-07, Observation of baryon-number violation, has a direct theoretical connection through monopole-induced nucleon decay. Some GUT monopoles are predicted to catalyze that process, but measuring magnetic charge would not demonstrate baryon-number violation. Conversely, observing baryon-number violation would not by itself identify a monopole. The two entries therefore retain distinct discovery requirements.

Roster-based synthesis: PHY-04, Laboratory identification of the dark-matter particle, and PHY-12, Experimental identification of the physics that sets the Higgs-mass scale, share the broader goal of identifying new microscopic physics. A monopole discovery would establish neither a dark-matter identity nor an explanation of the Higgs-mass scale without additional evidence. PHY-08, Observation of lepton-number violation, and PHY-13, A tested mechanism for the cosmic matter excess, likewise require their own symmetry-violation or cosmological demonstrations; none follows automatically from magnetic charge.

Roster-based synthesis: PHY-01, Ambient-pressure superconducting conductors at room temperature, concerns a different materials capability. Superconducting induction is a measurement tool in the monopole search, and this discovery criterion does not require room-temperature superconductivity. PHY-10, Collider-quality plasma wakefield acceleration, concerns accelerator performance. Improved accelerators could conditionally extend some production searches, but accelerator performance and monopole discovery remain separate achievements.

Scope distinction: emergent monopole-like excitations in materials, including the spin-ice comparison raised in the research, fall outside this free-particle discovery criterion. The supplied evidence does not establish their experimental history, so no claim that spin-ice monopoles have already been observed is adopted here. Their relevance is the distinction between an effective excitation in matter and the free magnetically charged particle targeted by PHY-06.

unresolved_issues: The contents, detailed scope and exact publication date of the cited 2025 MoEDAL full-detector Run 2 paper remain unverified in the supplied review.
The reported 2025 NOvA search has no supplied source, leaving its date, sensitivity, assumptions and outcome unverified here.
The exact 15 August 2024 journal publication date for the beam-pipe paper comes from supplied metadata rather than reviewed document contents.
The supplied record does not establish comprehensive monopole-search or discovery coverage through 1 November 2026.
Monopole masses, cosmic abundance and nucleon-decay catalysis remain theory-dependent; the supplied material does not resolve which scenario, if any, describes nature.
The experimental history of spin-ice monopole-like excitations is not documented by the supplied sources.

brief.title: Finding a particle with a lone magnetic pole
possible: Scientists could study a magnetic monopole: a free particle that acts as an isolated source of magnetic field. They could measure its magnetic charge and investigate its mass, interactions and origin.
why: Finding such a particle would establish magnetic charge as a property of matter. It would give physicists a way to investigate why electric charge comes in discrete amounts and test theories that predict magnetic particles.

sources.who: B. Acharya and collaborators in MoEDAL
sources.showed: MoEDAL scanned material from the CMS particle collider beam pipe for trapped monopoles and found no signal. The result ruled out some possibilities under assumptions about how monopoles form and become trapped.
sources.quote:
It was scanned by the MoEDAL experiment using a
SQUID magnetometer to search for trapped MMs. No MM signal was observed.
sources.cited_for: The search demonstrates a way to look for trapped magnetic charge and constrains some possible monopoles.
sources.not_established: It did not detect a monopole or rule out monopoles beyond its production and trapping assumptions.

sources.showed: This is a full-detector search reporting limits on possible monopoles.
sources.cited_for: It supports the case that collider searches constrain possible magnetic charges.
sources.not_established: Search limits do not establish a positive measurement of magnetic charge.

sources.showed: IceCube described an analysis still under development to search for slow monopoles through light from proton decays they might trigger. It also reported earlier limits that depend on how readily monopoles trigger those decays.
sources.quote:
Since 2012, a dedicated Slow-Particle Filter has been implemented
in the IceCube Neutrino Observatory for the detection of magnetic monopoles.
sources.cited_for: It supports a search route for slow cosmic monopoles and explains the dependence on assumed interactions.
sources.not_established: The developing analysis had not produced a completed search result, and its detection route depends on monopoles triggering proton decay.

shown: MoEDAL has searched collider material for trapped monopoles without finding a signal. Its detector offers a direct measurement route: a trapped monopole would leave a lasting electric current proportional to its magnetic charge.

IceCube has constrained the arrival rate of slow cosmic monopoles that could trigger proton decay. Its newer analysis remained under development. These results constrain particular possibilities without providing a reproducible magnetic-charge measurement.
missing: A positive magnetic-charge measurement that repeats reliably and rules out detector errors and other particles is still missing.
A monopole must be produced or encountered within a detector's reach; its mass and abundance remain unknown.
A convincing detection needs either a stable trapped-particle response or a track whose speed and other signals distinguish magnetic charge.

milestones.label: Reproducible magnetic charge in whole Dirac units
milestones.explanation: A free particle's measured magnetic charge would have to repeat and match a nonzero whole multiple of the Dirac unit, the theoretical basic magnetic charge. This would establish its defining property.

milestones.label: Repeated scans give the same trapped-particle charge
milestones.explanation: A trapped candidate would have to produce the same calibrated, lasting current on repeated scans through a detector with no electrical resistance. This would distinguish magnetic charge from spurious current changes.

milestones.label: Tracks distinguish magnetic charge from electric charge
milestones.explanation: A particle track with independently measured speed would have to yield a reproducible magnetic-charge measurement distinct from electrically charged particles. This would provide an alternative discovery route.

milestones.label: A discovery report defines what was measured
milestones.explanation: A report would have to specify charge, mass information, speed, detector coverage, interaction assumptions and remaining explanations. This would define what the discovery establishes and where its conclusions apply.

uncertain: The particle's mass, cosmic abundance and ability to trigger proton decay depend on which theory describes it.
Magnetic charge alone would not identify a theory that unifies the fundamental forces.
The proposed discovery criteria leave room for different forms of reproducibility, including repeated scans, additional events and independent detectors.

page.title: Observation of a free magnetic monopole
page.definition: A free magnetic monopole would be a particle that carries net magnetic charge and can exist in vacuum as an isolated source or sink of magnetic field. It could also carry electric charge, in which case it is called a dyon. Its magnetic charge could be identified in flight or after capture in matter. The monopoles imaged in spin ice are collective excitations of the material.

goal.need: Electric charge comes in discrete units. A free monopole would give a quantum-mechanical explanation for that regularity. Its magnetic charge would also test which global form of the Standard Model's gauge group describes nature. Four forms agree on the local interactions of known particles but allow different magnetic charges. A measured charge could rule out forms that forbid it. If several forms allow that charge, the ambiguity would remain.

statements.quote: Finding the minimum magnetic charge could provide a unique way to probe the structure of the gauge group.
The prime motivation of MOEDAL is to search directly for the magnetic monopole

completion.title: A direct observation of a particle's magnetic charge reaches at least 5σ significance.
completion.criterion: A direct particle observation identifies nonzero magnetic charge and reaches at least 5σ significance against the no-monopole background. The detector response must distinguish magnetic charge from electric charge, magnetic dipoles and instrumental signals. This applies the general particle-physics discovery convention to a magnetic-charge signal; it supplies no universal event count, charge precision or replication count.
completion.set_by: Particle-physics community convention, documented by CERN in “12 steps – From idea to discovery”, step 11; the magnetic-charge observable is described by the Particle Data Group.
completion.threshold_quote: A “discovery” is claimed when the statistical significance of the excess (the “bump”) is at least 5 sigma.
completion.basis: The 5σ threshold is the general particle-physics discovery convention. Magnetic charge gives the signal its physical interpretation. In 1982 Cabrera reported a superconducting-loop signal consistent with one Dirac charge in 151 days of observation and used the result to set a flux limit. The Particle Data Group's August 2025 review lists the early induction candidates as unconfirmed.

milestones.title: A magnetometer's magnetic-charge calibration is cross-checked with a pole of known strength.
milestones.criterion: Calibrate the magnetometer from measurements of a dipole of known magnetic moment. Cross-check the inferred response to magnetic charge with the end of a long, thin solenoid carrying a known current. Measure the reference dipole at the start of each run to monitor stability.
milestones.set_by: MoEDAL Collaboration, section 3 of its 2016 prototype trapping-detector paper; an apparatus-specific calibration check.
milestones.threshold_quote: cross-checked using long thin solenoids that mimic a monopole of well-known magnetic charge

milestones.title: A candidate track points to the collision point through all six sheets of one MoEDAL stack.
milestones.criterion: Identify an aligned entrance and exit pit in the first sheet of a six-sheet nuclear track detector. Examine the five downstream sheets and require an entrance and exit pit in each. All six pairs must lie on a common line pointing back to the collision point. This signature identifies a highly ionizing particle candidate.
milestones.set_by: MoEDAL Collaboration, candidate-track definition in its full-detector LHC Run 2 search; applies to the nuclear-track-detector route.
milestones.threshold_quote: A HIP “candidate track” requires collinear etch-pits pairs, pointing to the collision point, in all six NTD sheets in the stack.

milestones.title: A trapping sample gives the same nonzero magnetic charge on repeated passes through the magnetometer.
milestones.criterion: Measure the difference in current before and after the sample passes through the sensing coil, correcting for the empty holder. If the magnitude of the inferred charge exceeds 0.25 Dirac charges on the initial pass, scan the sample several more times. The repeat measurements must agree with a common nonzero charge of the same sign.
milestones.set_by: MoEDAL Collaboration, section 3 of its 2016 prototype trapping-detector paper; applies to trapped-particle induction measurements.
milestones.threshold_quote: A sample containing a genuine monopole would consistently yield the same value for repeated measurements

milestones.title: A signal identifying a particle's magnetic charge reaches at least 3σ evidence.
milestones.criterion: Identify a signal attributable to particles carrying magnetic charge and establish an excess with significance of at least 3σ against the expected background in the absence of monopoles.
milestones.set_by: Particle-physics community evidence convention, documented by CERN in “Why all this fuss over a few Sigma?”; applied here to magnetic-charge identification.
milestones.threshold_quote: Three sigma or more is considered evidence for a new phenomenon

not_found: No monopole-specific, detector-independent discovery criterion or fixed independent-replication count was found in the PDG, CERN or MoEDAL documents searched.
No common milestone sequence covering induction, track and cosmic searches was found; the detector milestones describe separate experimental routes.

results.finding: One SQUID magnetometer was calibrated for magnetic charge using two independent methods.
results.quote:
To calibrate the device’s
response to magnetic charge, two independent methods
were used, as described elsewhere [21, 43].

results.finding: MoEDAL scanned 57 CMS beam-pipe samples 6–12 times each and found no statistically significant signal.
results.quote:
A total of 57 tubes with each set
of fragments were passed through the SQUID multiple
times (6–12 times) to scan for the presence of magnetic
charges. Figure 3 shows the results. No statistically sig-
nificant signal was observed.

results.finding: MoEDAL cross-checked its dipole calibration with two solenoids and found run-start dipole readings consistent within 1%.
results.detail: Comparison of the independent calibration methods gave an estimated 10% uncertainty in the calibration constant.
results.quote: A calibration dipole sample of well-known magnetic moment was measured at the start of each run, with current values found to be consistent within 1%, ensuring that the calibration constant remained stable.

results.finding: All 12 MoEDAL aluminium samples flagged among 606 scanned gave repeat charge readings consistent with zero.
results.detail: The initial outliers were attributed to spurious SQUID current jumps.
results.quote: In all cases where the first measurement showed a large fluctuation, subsequent additional check measurements of the same sample were consistent with zero.

results.finding: MoEDAL cross-checked its SQUID calibration with two solenoids and measured reference dipole readings consistent within 1% across runs.
results.detail: Comparison of the independent calibration methods gave an estimated 10% uncertainty in the calibration constant.
results.quote:
A
calibration dipole sample of well-known magnetic moment was measured at the start of each
run, with current values found to be consistent within 1%, ensuring that the calibration
constant remained stable.

results.finding: Of 606 aluminium trapping samples, all 12 flagged for repeat SQUID scans gave readings consistent with zero on remeasurement.
results.detail: The paper attributes the initial readings to spurious magnetometer current jumps.
results.quote:
In all cases where the ﬁrst measurement
showed a large ﬂuctuation, subsequent additional check measurements of the same sample
were consistent with zero.
